name: Tooltip
summary: A short plain-text hint that describes a focusable control — 'Open application', 'Mark done (D)' — shown on keyboard focus and after a hover delay, dismissed with Escape. Supplementary by definition: the control must make sense without it, and an icon-only button keeps its aria-label. Never interactive content; a hint that needs a link or a button is a Popover.

pattern.name: Tooltip (WAI-ARIA role tooltip, WCAG 1.4.13 content on hover or focus)

trigger.intent: The focusable control the tooltip describes. React Aria adds aria-describedby to it while the tooltip is shown. Must be focusable — a tooltip on a static span is unreachable from the keyboard and therefore forbidden.

children.intent: The hint. Plain text, one line or two; no headings, links or controls. Read as the trigger's description, after its name.

placement.intent: Preferred side; flips when there is no room. Gap to the trigger is space.200, read from the token at runtime (shared with Popover).

showOn.intent: 'hover' shows on pointer hover AND on keyboard focus — the only mode that satisfies the no-hover-only rule. 'focus' shows on keyboard focus only, for triggers where hover would be noise. Maps to React Aria's trigger option; named showOn here because trigger is the element.

delay.intent: Hover warm-up in ms before the first tooltip appears (React Aria's global warm-up: once one is shown, siblings open instantly). Keyboard focus shows immediately regardless.

closeDelay.intent: ms the tooltip stays after the pointer leaves, so it can be moved onto the tooltip itself (WCAG 1.4.13 hoverable).

isDisabled.intent: Suppresses the tooltip without disabling the trigger.

isOpen.intent: Controlled visibility, for stories and tests. Normally uncontrolled.

onOpenChange.intent: Shown or hidden by any means.

showArrow.intent: A decorative arrow pointing at the trigger (OverlayArrow), in the tooltip's own surface colour.

keyboard.key: Tab / Shift+Tab (keyboard focus on the trigger)
keyboard.action: Shows the tooltip immediately — only for keyboard-visible focus, so a mouse click on the trigger does not flash it. Leaving the trigger hides it.
Hides the tooltip; focus stays on the trigger (WCAG 1.4.13 dismissable).
Shows after `delay`; stays while the pointer is over the trigger or the tooltip itself; hides `closeDelay` after it leaves (1.4.13 hoverable, persistent).

a11y.name: The tooltip has no name of its own and never names the trigger. It is the trigger's description (aria-describedby), read after the trigger's name. An icon-only trigger still needs aria-label.
a11y.announcements: role="tooltip"; aria-describedby is added to the trigger while shown, so on focus a screen reader reads the trigger's name, then the hint. Nothing is announced on hover alone.
a11y.targetSize: Not a target. The trigger is a Button and meets its own size; the tooltip never contains anything to press.

rules: Hover-only tooltips are forbidden (docs/ACCESSIBILITY.md): showOn='hover' also shows on keyboard focus, and the trigger must be focusable. A tooltip on a static element is a tooltip nobody on a keyboard can reach.
Supplementary, never load-bearing. The control must make sense without the hint, and an icon-only button keeps its aria-label — the tooltip describes, it does not name (4.1.2).
Plain text only. No links, buttons, inputs or headings inside; the pointer may move onto the tooltip to read it (1.4.13), not to use it. A hint that needs a control is a Popover.
WCAG 1.4.13, all three: dismissable (Escape, focus stays), hoverable (closeDelay lets the pointer reach it; hovering it keeps it open), persistent (stays until hover or focus leaves).
Shows on keyboard-visible focus only — a mouse click on the trigger does not flash it (React Aria's focus-visible logic). That is what makes a tooltip on every icon button tolerable.
Not on disabled controls: they receive neither focus nor hover, so the hint is unreachable. Put the explanation beside the control instead.
Inverse surface (color.surface.inverse / text.inverse — the pair the token layer defines for tooltips) and no border or shadow: the contrast with the page is the separation, on every theme.
One or two lines, 12 px caption text, max 320 px wide. If it needs more, it is not a tooltip.
No z-index token yet (PARKING.md); the portal's DOM order stacks it above page content.

examples.title: Shortcut hint
examples.code: <Tooltip trigger={<Button aria-label="Mark done: Email Priya">…</Button>} placement="bottom">Mark done (D)</Tooltip>

examples.title: Focus only
examples.code: <Tooltip trigger={<Button variant="tertiary">Stretch</Button>} showOn="focus">Counts against the 1-in-5 stretch quota</Tooltip>
